claims.text: Current-dollar (nominal) PCE increased $23.7 billion (0.1 percent) from the preceding month in July 2022.

citations.quotation: Disposable personal income (DPI) increased $37.6 billion (0.2 percent) and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $23.7 billion (0.1 percent).

claims.text: The nominal PCE increase reflected a $33.3 billion increase in services spending, partly offset by a $9.6 billion decrease in goods spending.

citations.quotation: $23.7 billion increase in current-dollar PCE in July reflected an increase of $33.3 billion in spending for services that was partly offset by a decrease of $9.6 billion in spending for goods (table 3).

claims.text: The personal saving rate was 5.0 percent, with personal saving of $932.3 billion in July.

citations.quotation: Personal saving was $932.3 billion in July and the personal saving rate—personal saving as a percentage of disposable personal income—was 5.0 percent (table 1).

claims.text: Nominal (current-dollar) spending is distinct from the PCE price index: while nominal PCE rose 0.1 percent, the PCE price index decreased 0.1 percent (and core PCE prices rose 0.1 percent); current-dollar estimates are valued at market prices of the transaction period, while real values are inflation-adjusted.

citations.quotation: The PCE price index decreased 0.1 percent. Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index increased 0.1 percent (table 9). Real DPI increased 0.3 percent in July and real PCE increased 0.2 percent

Current-dollar estimates are valued in the prices of the period when the transactions occurred—that is, at “market value.” Also referred to as “nominal estimates” or as “current-price estimates.” Real values are inflation-adjusted estimates—that is, estimates that exclude the effects of price changes.

counterarguments.text: One might interpret the PCE price index movement (-0.1 percent) as spending falling, but the source distinguishes nominal spending (up $23.7 billion, 0.1 percent) from prices; inflation-adjusted (real) PCE actually rose 0.2 percent.

citations.quotation: Real DPI increased 0.3 percent in July and real PCE increased 0.2 percent; goods increased 0.2 percent and services increased 0.2 percent (tables 5 and 7).

limitations: Excerpts are partial; full tables 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 not provided, so underlying values cannot be verified beyond quoted figures.
No calculation of the goods/services net change is performed; that would require summing the $33.3 billion increase in services and the $9.6 billion decrease in goods from the cited facts.
The release date (publication) is declared in the title but not verified; the data period is July 2022.
Monthly percent changes for goods and services in current dollars are not separately quoted (only real 0.2/0.2 percent and dollar amounts).
